doc.title: Joe Ascione interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001

title: First Fagen show at the Lone Star; Noel Redding trio
summary: The first Rock and Soul Revue show in New York, then a recent Hendrix-tune trio with Noel Redding and Eric Schenkman. He says labels are just for talking about music.

bands.name: Donald Fagen's Rock and Soul Revue

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah, the first show was in New York at the old Lone Star, the one with the iguana outside. And it was a real rush, it really was. That was the first experience I had like the whole group coming together and saying a prayer before going out in front of the — you know it was real hype type stuff. And you know thousands of people out there screaming “Fagan, yo, Steely Dan,” they were wanting this tune and that tune. We didn’t do those, we did other stuff. But it was great. No playing with people like that it’s fantastic. I just recently, well last year, did a gig with Noel Redding, Hendrix’s original bass player. So we did, like we were doing Hendrix tunes with Eric Schenkman, the guitarist who founded the Spin Doctors. So it was a power trio. Erick Schenkman from the Spin Doctors, and Noel Redding, and I’m playing drums. It was supposed to be Corky Lange from the old Mountain group who I’m friends with, but he couldn’t make it or whatever. So we’re playing Hendrix tunes and Beatle tunes and Mountain tunes and at one point I’m starting to weird out, like I’m saying this is Noel Redding, this is as close as I’ll ever get to meeting Hendrix you know. So it was a rush. It was great.
That’s so funny. Here you are playing—

Yeah and then you’re playing “Big Butter and Egg Man” from nineteen twenty something. And you know, well to me, just good music and not good music in any style. We just put labels on it so we could either talk about it or not talk about it. So yeah. No but I just like trying to play the instrument as well as I can and try to plug into musical situations and do as good a job as I can.
